lead: A loopback peer that answers a close by hanging up reads as a protocol error, not as the end.
body: `tungstenite` writes its close echo only on the next read, write or flush, so a peer thread that breaks out of its loop and drops the socket sends a bare FIN and the client's codec answers `ResetWithoutClosingHandshake`. A case asserting `null` after a close rests on the read loop in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/http/socket.rs` reading a failure after *this* end closed as the end; one about the *peer* closing has to make the peer flush first.
